work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
label: Samson the Nazirite
def: The Nazirite judge whose birth an angel announces, who tears a lion and later finds honey in its carcass, and who dies pulling down the pillars of the Philistine temple, killing more enemies in his death than in his life.
christ: Samson tearing the lion foreshadows Christ destroying death, and the honey in the carcass is the sweetness of life drawn out of it: "Samson the Nazarite shadowed forth a type of Thy working" (Ephrem, *Nativity* 8). His leaning on the two pillars shows "the mystery of Christ" (Irenaeus, *Fragment* 27).
where: Ephrem, *Hymns on the Nativity* 8 — “Samson the Nazarite shadowed forth a type of Thy working. He tore the lion, the image of death, whom Thou didst destroy”
Ephrem, *Hymns for the Epiphany* 2.25 — “In the honey of Samson--the nations tasted bitterness therein that destroyed them:--they had life in the Cross that redeemed them”
Augustine, *C. Faust.* 12.32 — “when he killed the lion that met him as he went to get a wife among strangers, but He who, when going to call His Church from among the Gentiles”
Ambrose, *De Spir. S.* 2 prol. 6 — “The people of the Gentiles which believed had honey, the people which was before savage is now the people of Christ.”
Ambrose, *De Spir. S.* 2 prol. 8 — “Grace came forth from the offence, power from weakness, and life from death.”
Irenaeus, *Fragment* 27 — “The fact, then, of Samson leaning himself upon the pillars, [indicates] this, that the people, when instructed, recognized the mystery of Christ.”
